- Snowfall is willing to sign an SLA amendment that includes operational runbook and monitoring obligations on both sides.

Can your team confirm feasibility (observability and infra constraints) and propose the next steps? If necessary we can accept a staged commitment (e.g., 50ms P95 for first 3 months while we run a warm capacity ramp).

Thanks —

Quick asks for each:
- Marissa (Product/Infra): is sub-50ms P95 realistic for these endpoints given our current models, typical sequence lengths, and routing layers? If not achievable, please propose the minimum technical carveouts (dedicated pool size, model variant, caching strategy) and the expected P95 we can guarantee.
- Sean (SRE/Operations): what observability and alerting hooks do we need in the amendment? They want an ops runbook — please prepare a 1-2 page runbook snippet we can attach. Also call out fallback behavior (what we do when latency/throughput spikes).

Tentative approach (my recommendation): dedicated reserved pool + prefix/KV caching + model quantization where appropriate, plus a staged SLO (50ms P95 for first 90 days during ramp, target sub-50ms thereafter). If we can hit 50ms across realistic inputs, we have a stronger commercial position.

Please respond with feasibility and a proposed set of technical/commercial options by EOD 24 Nov so I can get back to Jen with a concrete plan.

Hannah / team — quick technical readout after a half-day spike sim and model profiling. Notes below and attached snippets (ops_runbook_snippets.txt).

Findings:
- Endpoints: image-embed-v2 (median tokens small; compute-bound), text-rank-v1 (longer sequences)
- Baseline (multi-tenant): p95 ~72ms for image-embed-v2, ~120ms for text-rank-v1 under our typical routing and load.

Proposed configuration to get to sub-50ms P95 on image-embed-v2 and as-close-as-possible on text-rank-v1:
1) Dedicated reserved pool (suggest 6x H100-equivalent slots for image-embed-v2 traffic; 8x for text-rank-v1 if they want both at sub-50ms).
2) Model variant: use int8 quantized image-embed-v2 (verified accuracy retention on our eval set). For text-rank-v1 we recommend an optimized mid-size variant plus KV cache priming.
3) Prefix/KV caching: require Snowfall to send warmup traffic during scheduled windows; we'll provide a cache-priming script.
4) Traffic shaping and burst allowance: cap burst QPS beyond committed capacity; automated fallback to slightly higher-latency model when spikes exceed threshold.

Operational guarantees we can commit to (subject to legal wording):
- Uptime: standard SLA for availability.
- Latency: dedicate the above config and guarantee sub-50ms P95 for image-embed-v2 under committed capacity and normal sequence lengths; for text-rank-v1 we can commit to 85ms P95 under committed capacity.
- Runbook: attached short snippets for warmup, cache priming, and escalation play.

Caveats: long-tail requests (very long sequences) and cross-region traffic will not be included. We should include clear exclusion language in the amendment.

Next steps: I can turn this into a short technical annex for the SLA amendment. If Sales/Legal agree on the commitment levels above (image-embed-v2 sub-50ms; text-rank-v1 85ms), I'll assemble a final ops appendix and hand to Priya for the commercial doc.

Marissa Cole
Director, Product Ops | Redwood Inference
